what_changed: Added merge-on-write: session-owned fields (owner, attempts, retry_budget, blocked_evidence), session-set states, unknown keys and hand-added entries all survive a re-score; entry ids are assigned once per route and persisted instead of being positional.
why: PD-003 and PD-004 in receipt CYC-0001. Step 3 of every cycle ran --write, which regenerated the ledger from the graph and destroyed the loop's only memory on a four-hour cadence, and positional ids meant a receipt's entry id would later name a different route.
old_value: --write rebuilt all entries from systems/graph and wrote them over the existing file; ids were AUT-{sorted index + 1}.
new_value: merge(generated, existing) preserves session state and hand-added rows; ids are stable per route.
self_serving_check: NO, and the opposite. It makes the loop's own attempts and fruitless-attempt penalty actually accumulate, so routes the loop keeps failing at will DECAY in priority rather than resetting to a clean slate every cycle. It also makes blocked_evidence durable, which is what CLAUDE.md §0 requires before a block may stand.

what_changed: Added six guards for PD-003 and PD-004: a hand-added entry survives a re-score; a claim survives the next re-score; blocked_evidence is never discarded; an entry id is stable when the graph grows; a new route gets an unused id; and a mutation test that bypasses merge() and asserts the preservation actually breaks.
why: The fix for PD-003/PD-004 is worthless without guards — both defects were silent, and a silent defect that returns is indistinguishable from one that never left.
old_value: 8 tests covering the scorer's clamps only.
new_value: 14 tests; the six new ones cover ledger persistence and id stability.
self_serving_check: NO — every one of the six ADDS a constraint on the loop. None relaxes an assertion, none deletes a case, and the mutation test exists specifically to prove the new guards are not decorative. Declared because tests/** is a governed path and the guard correctly refused the commit until it was.

what_changed: Added the term `blocked_with_evidence` (-90) and `prerequisite_bonus` (0.5).
why: CYC-0001 established the top-scored item as blocked WITH evidence, and it still scored 195 and still sorted first — so the next cycle would have re-derived the identical block every four hours forever. And the two artifacts that would clear it scored null, so the driver could never have taken them. Both found by running the contract, not by reading it.
old_value: No penalty for an evidenced block; no way for unblocking work to inherit priority.
new_value: An evidenced block costs 90; a prerequisite inherits its parent's pre-penalty score plus 0.5 so it sorts immediately above what it unblocks.
self_serving_check: NO. The penalty makes the loop STAND DOWN from work it has proven it cannot currently do, which reduces what it can claim to be working on. The bonus promotes the harder, slower job (a hardening round and a blind seat) over the easy one (posting), which is the opposite of making success easier to report.

what_changed: Five more guards: an evidenced block leaves the top of the queue; a prerequisite outranks what it unblocks; a prerequisite inherits the parent's PRE-penalty value; a hand-filed row never steals a derived row's id; every derived entry carries the _derived mark.
why: Three of the five bind bugs that were live in this session, including one I introduced while fixing another — the merge's route map let a hand-filed row hand its id to the graph's row for that route, so 'escalate the emails' became 'post the preprint'.
old_value: 14 tests.
new_value: 19 tests.
self_serving_check: NO — all five add constraints. None relaxes an assertion or deletes a case. ⚠ And the weight-declaration test caught my own new term being read through a different expression than every other one; I changed the CODE to match rather than loosening the test, which is the direction that rule exists to force.

what_changed: §10.2 corrected a second time: fire_trigger also refuses a UI-created Routine, so an agent has NO control over one from outside it — not the prompt, not the cron, not a manual fire. Only a session that Routine itself fired may act on it, and only to disable.
why: Tried to fire the driver on demand to prove the chain 55 minutes early. Refused: 'Agents can only fire routines they created.' The row had said fire was allowed, written from what the tool description implies rather than from a call.
old_value: Fire a Routine off-schedule: allowed. Disable: allowed.
new_value: Fire: refused for http_api routines. Disable: only from a session that routine itself fired.
self_serving_check: NO — it REMOVES a capability the loop was documented as having, which narrows what it can do unattended. ⚠ Worth recording that this row was wrong twice in one afternoon in the SAME direction, both times from reading a tool description instead of making a call. The correction is the rule, not the row: an unexercised capability is UNKNOWN, not available.

what_changed: New guard: every S3 prefix written on the expiring SageMaker bucket must be claimed by archive-results-aws.yml's DEFAULT_PREFIXES, the archiver must carry a schedule, and every exemption must state a reason. Five tests including a mutation test.
why: Root cause of AUT-INC-001. The archiver exists BECAUSE 'old outputs were lost to S3 lifecycle expiration' (its own header) — and it was left dispatch-only with a prefix list that covered NONE of the six prefixes the repo writes to today. nr4a3-step1-fanout was never in it, which is why ~8,500 objects expired with no mirror.
old_value: No guard; coverage of the archiver was whatever anyone remembered to add.
new_value: A predicate-scoped test plus a weekly schedule on the archiver.
self_serving_check: NO — it adds a constraint that can FAIL the build on work the loop does later, and it obliges every future lane to declare itself. It makes the repo harder to add to, deliberately. Scoped to a PREDICATE rather than a list precisely because a list is what drifted (paper-hardening: a fix scoped to a LIST regresses at a sibling).

what_changed: Added claim_lease.periods = 2. A claim (`owner`) now expires after two cycle periods and the item returns to the queue; an owner with no claimed_utc is stale immediately.
why: A LIVE STALL, found in the committed ledger: CYC-0003 claimed AUT-PROP-002, completed its cycle, and never released the claim. merge() faithfully carries `owner` across every re-score and nothing ever cleared one, so the claim was permanent — the next driver would skip the queue's top item, silently, every four hours, forever. A cycle killed mid-item produces the identical state and announces nothing.
old_value: No lease. A claim was a deed.
new_value: A claim is a lease with an expiry, and an unstamped claim fails toward release.
self_serving_check: NO — it takes work AWAY from a cycle's exclusive hold and returns it to contention, and it increments attempts on release so a repeatedly-abandoned item DECAYS in priority. It makes the loop's grip on work weaker, not stronger.

what_changed: Added an eighth condition, queue_is_takeable: is there ANY item a cycle could actually pick up (unowned, not retry-exhausted, scored)?
why: Every other condition asks whether the loop works WELL. None asked whether there is work it CAN do. A queue where everything is owned, blocked or out of retry budget produces a loop that fires on schedule, finds nothing, writes a receipt saying so, and repeats — indistinguishable from a healthy loop on a slow week.
old_value: Seven conditions.
new_value: Eight; the new one counts what a cycle would TAKE, not what exists.
self_serving_check: NO — a new way for the board to go red is a new way for the loop to be told to stop and escalate. It cannot make any existing check easier to pass.

what_changed: Step 4 now requires stamping claimed_utc and explains the lease; step 9 requires releasing the claim; the refusal table gains a row for an untakeable queue.
why: The lease is the backstop for a cycle that DIED. A cycle that lived and did not release is leaving litter for the backstop to clean, and 'fire, find nothing, write a receipt saying so' is precisely what a stalled loop does forever.
old_value: Claim with owner only; no release step; no untakeable-queue refusal.
new_value: Stamp, release, and refuse to spin on an empty queue.
self_serving_check: NO — all three ADD obligations to a cycle. The new refusal row in particular forbids the easiest possible cycle (do nothing, report nothing to do), which is the one a lazy loop would prefer.

what_changed: New: 14 guards on the lease and the alarm, including that a fresh claim survives, an unparseable stamp releases, the committed ledger holds no immortal claims, the alarm stays silent on one transient red, does NOT re-alarm every run, and runs on the Actions clock rather than in a research cycle.
why: A lease and an alarm that are not tested are decorations, and the alarm's failure mode is the one that killed every previous push channel in this repo (1,476 commits in 24 h from a supervisor with nothing to supervise).
old_value: No coverage of either mechanism.
new_value: 14 tests.
self_serving_check: NO — every one constrains the loop. test_it_does_not_re_alarm_every_run in particular exists to stop the loop making itself ignorable.

what_changed: Updated the condition-count expectations from 7 to 8 for the declared queue_is_takeable row; changed the _lab fixture's default ledger from EMPTY to one takeable item; added two scenarios — an empty ledger is a measured stall, and a queue where everything is claimed is a stall.
why: The eighth condition correctly fired on a fixture whose default was an empty ledger. An empty ledger is not neutral scenery — it is a loop that fires on schedule and does nothing forever — so leaving it as the default would have made a stall the baseline of every test in the file.
old_value: Seven conditions asserted; _lab defaulted to entries: [].
new_value: Eight asserted; _lab carries one takeable item; the empty and all-claimed cases have their own tests.
self_serving_check: ⚠ THE HONEST ANSWER IS PARTLY YES AND IT IS WORTH SAYING SO: I edited tests that my own change had just turned red, which is the shape amendment_guard exists to catch. What makes it permissible is the DIRECTION — the check was not weakened. The strict reading (an empty ledger is red) was kept and given two dedicated tests; only the fixture's idea of 'neutral' changed. The alternative, softening queue_is_takeable to call an empty ledger 'unmeasured', was available and was refused: that would have been the goalpost move.

what_changed: Added the ninth condition, c_cycles_are_sized: groups receipts by session_id and goes red when one session carries more than autonomy-state.json's max_cycles_per_session. Unstamped receipts count as unmeasured, never as fresh sessions.

new_value: Nine conditions; the session-shape rule is measured for the first time.
why: trimcrae, 2026-08-26: 'Isn't there supposed to be rules about using subagents and starting new sessions to keep context from inflating? I know I asked for it. But that guard failed based on what I'm seeing in this thread.' He was right, and the root cause is worse than non-compliance: the rule was UNREACHABLE. It lived only in .claude/skills/research-loop/SKILL.md s3; a skill binds only when loaded; every one of that skill's four load triggers was a Routine firing a cycle. On the interactive path -- a human asking for research work directly -- the skill never loaded and s3 never applied. DISCRIMINATING OBSERVATION: '"name":"Skill"' appears 0 times in the offending session's transcript, which ran CYC-0005 and CYC-0006 end to end, carried 23 compaction markers and reached 7.6 MB; an earlier session ran three cycles against a cap of two.
self_serving_check: NO, and the direction is the test: every edit here makes the loop HARDER to run unchecked, not easier. A condition was ADDED (the board can now go red where it could not before), a cap was ADDED, a tripwire was ADDED to the file that loads every session, and the skill's load triggers were WIDENED so the rule binds on more paths rather than fewer. Nothing was loosened, no threshold was raised, and no failing check was edited to pass. The board goes RED on the real repository the moment this lands -- session_011zRMmQKPj7ziG3gY9yhpBQ ran 3 cycles against the cap -- which is the opposite of a self-serving change: it convicts the sessions that wrote it. The one thing that IS in the caught-shape: three shape tests asserting a typed count of 8 were rebound to len(CONDITION_ORDER). That is a one-fact-one-place fix, not a weakening -- the contract test that is MEANT to notice a new condition still asserts the exact key set by name, and mutation testing confirms both halves are load-bearing (un-wiring the condition: 3 tests red; deleting the rule text from CLAUDE.md: 1 test red).

what_changed: Added the tenth condition, c_fanout_is_governed: reads receipts' subagents.max_concurrent against autonomy-state.json's subagent_width. A receipt with no subagents block is UNMEASURED, never green.
old_value: Nine conditions; subagent_width was read by no code path in the repository.
new_value: Ten conditions; the width dial is measured for the first time.
why: trimcrae, 2026-08-26: 'Are we following our own rules about the optimal number of parallel subagents right now? If not, let's build that enforcement better.' MEASURED ANSWER: numerically yes (2 concurrent against subagent_width=5 at backoff_level 0), procedurally NO -- the cap was never read before either dispatch, so compliance was luck. And the enforcement was worse than the session-shape rule fixed one cycle earlier: 'grep -rn subagent_width' over the whole repository returned TWO hits, the JSON defining it and one test asserting it equals 5. No code read it; zero of seven receipts recorded a dispatch in any structured field. Architecture s9 calls this the most important dial and records why: a 107-agent fan-out hit the account weekly limit, 40 completed, 67 errored, the synthesis step failed and returned a truncation artifact.
self_serving_check: NO. Every edit makes the loop harder to run unchecked: a condition was ADDED so the board can go red where it could not before, the cap's unit was DEFINED so it is enforceable at all, and CLAUDE.md now names a limit at the exact line that previously granted unbounded spawn authority. Nothing was loosened and no threshold was raised. ONE SHAPE WORTH NAMING: the cap was not changed to fit what this session had already spent -- 5 is unchanged, and the guard's own remedy text is asserted by a test to say 'never widen the cap', because s8b.1e records that a guard whose printed remedy is the wrong fix teaches the wrong fix. The retroactive `subagents` block added to CYC-0006 records a dispatch that genuinely happened (2 blind seats on 34264bb, verifiable in that commit's seat records) and is flagged `_recorded_retroactively` rather than presented as contemporaneous. Mutation-tested four ways -- un-wiring the condition, hardcoding the cap, removing it from CLAUDE.md, and un-defining the unit -- all four caught. The board is NOT green after this change: cycles_are_sized still convicts this session.

self_serving_check.question: Does this change make it easier for me to report success?
self_serving_check.answer: NO, AND ONE DECISION INSIDE IT IS THE PROOF. The paper's measured coverage did NOT move (57/271 before and after) because `claim_coverage.py` discards a harvested pattern matching more than 10 % of a document's sentences and the identifier pattern matches 28 against a ceiling of 27 — one sentence. Raising MAX_MATCH_SHARE to 0.11 would have turned this cycle's work into a coverage gain. It was considered and REFUSED: `research-loop` §6 forbids changing a bar by the cycle it blocked, and the ceiling is doing exactly the job it was written for. Everything added here is an assertion that can only fail; no threshold, floor or existing assertion was weakened.

Three of round 27's five blind seats reached that sentence independently, from three unrelated lenses (regression off round 26's diff, statistics off the interval arithmetic, arithmetic off the source verbatim). self_serving_check: ⭐ ANSWERED, INCLUDING THE CASE AGAINST. THE CASE AGAINST: this cycle changed an assertion that would have gone red on this cycle's own edit, which is the shape research-loop §6 exists to catch, and 'the guard was wrong' is exactly what a cycle gaming a guard would also say. WHY IT IS NOT THAT, on evidence rather than assertion: (1) NOTHING WAS WEAKENED — the assertion still requires the floor's reason to be stated, still requires it to name the seven-to-ten comparison, and the added comment forbids the next re-anchor from dropping the range, so the guard is strictly more constraining than before. (2) THE FINDING IS NOT THE LOOP'S — it came from three blind seats that could not see each other or this cycle's intentions, and paper-hardening calls independent convergence the strongest signal this process produces. (3) THE ALTERNATIVE IS WORSE AND IS THE SELF-SERVING ONE — leaving the sentence alone keeps a false statement in a paper that is about to be posted, purely to avoid touching a test, which is a guard enforcing an error. (4) THE DIRECTION IT PROTECTS IS UNTOUCHED: 'floor' is still the word, and it is still true for the same reason — the criterion demands the most the enzyme is reported to need, so a run shorter than ten that could still license cleavage goes uncounted. ⚠ WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM: that a wording guard is a good instrument for a claim's direction. In an ordinary checkout `--absolute-git-dir` resolves to `<repo>/.git`, so the path is byte-identical and no baseline is lost. The hook's repo-finding loop eleven lines above already worked around exactly this (`[ -d "$cand/.git" ] || git -C "$cand" rev-parse --git-dir`); the state path then hardcoded the form the loop had just avoided. The place this disabled the guard is not exotic: `aso_archive_manifest.py --check-archive` refuses unless the tree is clean apart from the manifest, so regenerating it can ONLY be done in a pristine linked worktree — applied five times in this session alone. The repository sends sessions into the one environment where its own stall guard was off.
